top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rests on three separable, load-bearing contributions: the time-dependent pricing friction, staggered contracts with the policy rule, and the welfare-based synthesis. The work is mature (25 to 40 years old), has been revised rather than abandoned after 2008, the zero lower bound and the 2021-23 inflation, and has the broadest influence on both research and policy. As far as the supplied round-2 files show, no earlier prize recognised the pricing-friction and policy-rule core. Attribution remains the main cost, because the three-name cap excludes Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler. A citation limited to nominal rigidities, policy rules and the micro-founded synthesis reduces that cost but does not remove it. I rank P002 (Kiyotaki-Moore) second as a mature mechanism with clean attribution and a narrower footprint, and a close alternative. I rank no award last because both proposals are scientifically substantial.
recusal_note: No link to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki or Moore is apparent from the profile. I am a frequent co-author of Per Krusell (secretary) and John Hassler (chair) and an IIES colleague of both. Both support P001, so my ranking may be influenced by proximity, though I have tried to rest it on the arguments. My long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow (B013) is not relevant to any proposal on this slate. My profile weakly suggests, as an inference only, that I may have helped draft the 2025 Scientific Background. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
